item.intervention: Al mole fraction varied from 0 to 2
item.structure_change: Phase stability changes: A1 for x < 0.5, A1+A2 for 0.5 ≤ x ≤ 1.25, A2 for x > 1.25
item.property_change: Formation enthalpies positive for A1 and A2 phases, implying clustering expected
item.attributed_mechanism: Positive formation enthalpies of A1 and A2 phases imply clustering is expected in the HEA
quotes: A1 for x < 0.5, A1 + A2 for 0.5 ≤ Al ≤1.25, and A2 for Al > 1.25.
While the A1 phase is more stable than A2 for smaller x , the positive formation enthalpies of A1 and A2 phases imply that clustering is expected in the HEA.
Our findings are in agreement with experimental observations [24] and semi-empirical CALPHAD calculations [29] , especially for x = 0.1.

item.processing: MD simulations with strain rate 10^10 s^-1
item.test_conditions: Temperatures 77 K, 300 K, 700 K, 1,000 K; strain up to 0.9%
item.structure_change: Clustering-to-ordering transition occurs with increase in unlike pair correlations (Al-Co, Al-Cr) and decrease in like pair correlations (Al-Al)
item.property_change: Peak flow stress ~125 MPa at 77 and 300 K; ~90 MPa at 700 and 1,000 K; thermo-plastic instability causes thermal softening
item.attributed_mechanism: High-strain compression promotes atomistic rearrangements in Al0.1CrCoFeNi, resulting in a clustering-to-ordering transition
quotes: For compressive loading, a peak flow stress of ~125 MPa is recorded at 77 and 300 K, while it is ~90 MPa at 700 and 1,000 K.

Under compressive loading the clustering to ordering transition occurs with the increase in unlike pair correlations (e.g., Al-Co andAl-Cr) and decrease in like pair correlations (e.g., Al-Al), Fig. 9 .
